draft.title: Obtuse angles and supplementary angles
card: An obtuse angle is between \(90^{\circ}\) and \(180^{\circ}\). Its supplement is \(180^{\circ} - \theta\), and the two angles add to \(180^{\circ}\).
On the unit circle, the angles \(\theta\) and \(180^{\circ} - \theta\) give points mirrored across the y-axis. They have the same height and opposite x-values.

So \(\sin(180^{\circ} - \theta) = \sin \theta\) and \(\cos(180^{\circ} - \theta) = -\cos \theta\). An obtuse angle has a positive sine and a negative cosine. Example: \(\sin 150^{\circ} = \sin 30^{\circ} = \frac{1}{2}\), and \(\cos 150^{\circ} = -\cos 30^{\circ}\).
For complementary angles, which add to \(90^{\circ}\), \(\sin \theta = \cos(90^{\circ} - \theta)\). Example: \(\sin 20^{\circ} = \cos 70^{\circ}\).
draft.remember: Sine stays the same and cosine changes sign when you use \(180^{\circ}\) minus the angle.

a.why: An obtuse angle has a positive sine and a negative cosine, because its point is above the x-axis and to the left of the y-axis. The option with the signs swapped confuses which coordinate is which.
a.clue: Sine is the height of the point. Cosine is its x-value.

b.q: Given that \(\sin 35^{\circ} \approx 0.57\), which of these is also about 0.57?
b.why: The supplement of \(35^{\circ}\) is \(145^{\circ}\), and \(\sin 145^{\circ} = \sin 35^{\circ}\). \(\cos 145^{\circ}\) is \(-\cos 35^{\circ}\), which is negative, so it is a tempting but wrong choice. \(\sin 55^{\circ} = \cos 35^{\circ}\), which is not 0.57.
b.clue: Find the supplement of \(35^{\circ}\), and check the sign.
